2

6	import yaml, argparse

13	
14	Goal: replicate exactly with pure Node.js ESM (`.mjs`), zero external modules.
15	HARD CONSTRAINTS for all code: no `JSON.*` calls, no regular expressions
16	(no `/.../` literals, no `new RegExp`, no `.match/.search/.replace/.split` with a
17	regex argument — string arguments are fine), no npm imports, only relative local
18	imports with full `.mjs` suffix and `node:` builtins.
19	
20	Reference executable for black-box probing: `/workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a 'VALUE'`
21	(never use the `python` command). Note: `print(result)` where result ends in `\n`
22	means the program output ends with a blank line.
23	
24	## Module layout (all under /output)
25	
26	- `lib/yamlTypes.mjs` — already written; exports `class YamlTimestamp { constructor(text){ this.text = text } }`.
27	- `lib/yamlParser.mjs` — `export function safeLoad(text)` → JS value:
28	  `null | boolean | number | string | YamlTimestamp | Array | plain Object`.
29	  Throws `Error` on malformed YAML (caller exits 1).
30	- `lib/yamlDumper.mjs` — `export function dump(value)` → string (ends with `\n`;
31	  includes the `...\n` document-end marker where PyYAML emits one).
32	- `lib/argparse.mjs` — `export function parseArgs(argv)` → `{ a }`; mimics Python argparse.
33	- `test4.mjs` — entry: parseArgs(process.argv) → safeLoad → dump → console.log(result);
34	  catch parse errors: write message to stderr, `process.exit(1)`.
35	
36	## Observed behavior (black-box probes)
37	
38	### Argument parsing (argparse replica)
39	- `--a VALUE` and `--a=VALUE` both accepted; `--a` is required.
40	- prog name = basename of script (for the executable it prints `test4_executable`;
41	  our entry should use basename of `process.argv[1]`, i.e. `test4.mjs`).
42	- Missing `--a`: stderr `usage: PROG [-h] --a A\nPROG: error: the following arguments are required: --a`, exit 2.
43	- `--a` with no value, or value that looks like an option (starts with `-` and is NOT
44	  a negative number like `-42`): stderr `... error: argument --a: expected one argument`, exit 2.
45	  (`--a -42` works and parses `-42`; `--a --` and `--a -.inf` fail; `--a=-.inf` fails too
46	  because `-.inf` looks like an option... actually `--a=-.inf` also failed — so for `--a=X`
47	  form the same looks-like-option check applies.)
48	- Unknown args: stderr `... error: unrecognized arguments: --foo 1`, exit 2.
49	- `-h` / `--help`: prints help to stdout, exit 0:
50	  ```
51	  usage: PROG [-h] --a A
52	
53	  options:
54	    -h, --help  show this help message and exit
55	    --a A
56	  ```
57	- Abbreviated long options (argparse allow_abbrev): `--` prefix unambiguous match works
58	  in Python; low priority, optional.
59	
60	### YAML load (safe_load subset)
61	- Implicit scalar resolution (YAML 1.1, PyYAML rules):
62	  - null: `~`, `null`, `Null`, `NULL`, empty scalar → null.
63	  - bool: `yes/Yes/YES/no/No/NO/true/True/TRUE/false/False/FALSE/on/On/ON/off/Off/OFF`.
64	    (`y`/`n` are plain strings.)
65	  - int: `[-+]?[0-9]+`, with `_` separators (`1_000` → 1000), `0x` hex, `0o`/`0`-prefix
66	    octal, `0b` binary, sexagesimal `1:30` → 90 (base-60 groups, also floats `1:30.5`).
67	  - float: requires a dot: `1.`, `1.5`, `.5`, optional exponent (`1.5e3`); also
68	    `.inf`, `-.inf`, `+.inf`, `.Inf` etc, `.nan`. `1e3` (no dot) is a STRING.
69	  - timestamp: `2020-01-01` or `2001-12-15T02:59:43.1Z`-style → wrap in `YamlTimestamp`
70	    keeping the original text.
71	- Tags: `!!bool true`, `!!int 123`, `!!str 123`, `!<tag:yaml.org,2002:str> string`,
72	  `!!float`, `!!null`, `!!seq`, `!!map` — handle the common `tag:yaml.org,2002:*` set.
73	- Quoted scalars: single (`''` escape doubling) and double (`\n`, `\xNN`, `\uNNNN`, ...).
74	- Block mappings/sequences by indentation; flow collections `[1, 2]`, `{a: 1}`;
75	  comments `#`; blank lines; `---` / `...` document markers; anchors `&a` / aliases `*a`
76	  (alias resolves to same value); merge keys optional.
77	- Block scalars `|` literal and `>` folded with chomping indicators `+`/`-` and explicit
78	  indentation indicators — implement the common cases.
79	- Multi-line plain and quoted scalars (continuation lines more indented than the key).
80	- Duplicate mapping keys: LAST value wins, no error.
81	- Empty input or whitespace-only → null.
82	- Nested seq under map key is indentless on load too: `items:\n- 1\n- 2` works.
83	- Invalid YAML (e.g. `a: [1,2`) → the Python program exits with code 1 (traceback on
84	  stderr; exact traceback text does NOT need to match).
85	
86	### YAML dump (PyYAML dump, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=True, allow_unicode=False)
87	- Mapping keys are SORTED (`b,a` → `a,b`); numeric keys sorted numerically (`2` before `10`).
88	- Indent 2; sequences are INDENTLESS under mapping keys:
89	  `items:\n- 1\n- 2`; nested maps under `- ` items: `- b:\n    c: 1`.
90	- Top-level scalar output: `VALUE\n...\n`. Top-level empty map: `{}\n`; empty list: `[]\n`.
91	  Nested empty collections: `a: {}` / `a: []`.
92	- Non-scalar top-level output has NO `...` marker, just trailing `\n`.
93	- Scalar emission:
94	  - bool → `true`/`false`; null → `null`; int → decimal.
95	  - float: Python repr style — `1.0` (always a dot), `1.5`, `.inf`, `-.inf`, `.nan`,
96	    exponential like `1e+16` (two-digit exponent `1e-05`) for very large/small.
97	  - `YamlTimestamp` → its original text, plain.
98	  - strings: PLAIN when safe; SINGLE-QUOTED when the string would re-resolve to a
99	    non-str tag (`'123'`, `'true'`, `'null'`, `'yes'`, timestamp-like), or has
100	    leading/trailing space (`' x'`, `'x '`), or contains `: ` / ` #` (`'a: b'`, `'a # b'`),
101	    or starts with an indicator char (`-`, `?`, `:`, `!`, `&`, `*`, `#`, `{`, `}`, `[`,
102	    `]`, `,`, `|`, `>`, `@`, backtick, quotes...) in a way that would misparse;
103	    empty string → `''`. Inside single quotes, `'` doubles.
104	  - DOUBLE-QUOTED when the string contains non-ASCII or control characters
105	    (`héllo` → `"h\xE9llo"`): escapes `\xNN` (≤0xFF), `\uNNNN` (≤0xFFFF), `\UNNNNNNNN`,
106	    plus `\n \t \\ \" \0 \a \b \v \f \r \e`.
107	  - Strings containing newlines use SINGLE-QUOTED multi-line style: `"a\nb"` →
108	    `'a\n\n  b'` (newline becomes a blank line, continuation indented 2).
109	  - Plain scalars wider than 80 columns are FOLDED at spaces; continuation lines get
110	    2 extra spaces of indent:
111	    `...folded\n  at width eighty chars`.
112	- Mapping keys use the same scalar emission rules (quoted when needed: `'a b'` would be
113	  plain `a b:` since plain is safe there — probe showed `"a b"` key → `a b: 1`).
114	- Mixed-type mapping keys (int + str) → Python raises TypeError → program exits 1.
115

#!/bin/bash
# Differential test: /output/lib/argparse.mjs vs /workspace/dataset/test4_executable
# Prog names differ (test4_executable vs test4.mjs); normalize both to PROG.
cd /workspace/dataset
pass=0; fail=0

norm() { sed -e "s/test4_executable/PROG/g" -e "s/test4\.mjs/PROG/g"; }

run_case() {
  local desc="$1"; shift
  ./test4_executable "$@" >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; local refcode=$?
  node /tmp/driver.mjs "$@" >/tmp/my.out 2>/tmp/my.err; local mycode=$?
  # For successful parses, the executable prints YAML dump; we print A= value.
  # Compare: for exit 0 cases, check the executable's dump corresponds to the
  # same raw string (we instead verify exit codes + error text; value checks
  # are done separately in the value test below).
  local ok=1
  if [ "$refcode" != "$mycode" ]; then ok=0; fi
  if ! diff <(norm </tmp/ref.err) <(norm </tmp/my.err) >/dev/null; then ok=0; fi
  if [ "$refcode" != 0 ]; then
    if ! diff <(norm </tmp/ref.out) <(norm </tmp/my.out) >/dev/null; then ok=0; fi
  else
    # help case: stdout must match exactly (after prog normalization)
    if head -1 /tmp/ref.out | grep -q '^usage:'; then
      if ! diff <(norm </tmp/ref.out) <(norm </tmp/my.out) >/dev/null; then ok=0; fi
    fi
  fi
  if [ $ok = 1 ]; then pass=$((pass+1)); else
    fail=$((fail+1))
    echo "FAIL: $desc  (args: $*)"
    echo "  ref exit=$refcode my exit=$mycode"
    echo "  ref.err: $(norm </tmp/ref.err | tr '\n' '|')"
    echo "  my.err : $(norm </tmp/my.err | tr '\n' '|')"
    echo "  ref.out: $(norm </tmp/ref.out | tr '\n' '|')"
    echo "  my.out : $(norm </tmp/my.out | tr '\n' '|')"
  fi
}

# We infer the executable's received value only for simple strings via its YAML

  node /tmp/driver.mjs "$@" 2>/dev/null | head -1
